start_codegen_session.rationale: Starts local recording: `Start a new code generation session to record Playwright actions`. It writes session state and records the requested local `outputPath`, but the description does not say it returns page data or sends data to an attacker-readable destination. The later tools require a session `ID`, so the result is treated as providing `sessionId`.

end_codegen_session.rationale: It will `generate the test file` for a session that `record[ed] Playwright actions`; recorded actions may include private user/account data or attacker-authored page data. The advertised text does not specify whether generated content or only a path is returned, so SECRET/UNTRUSTED are kept under the least-restrictive reading.

get_codegen_session.rationale: It can `Get information about a code generation session`; because sessions `record Playwright actions`, that information may include private interactions or attacker-authored page-derived identifiers/text. The exact output fields are not advertised, so labels are kept as undetermined.

clear_codegen_session.rationale: It `Clear[s] a code generation session without generating a test`, changing only local session state identified by `sessionId`; no return of external content or attacker-readable delivery is advertised.

playwright_navigate.rationale: It can `Navigate to a URL` supplied as `url`, causing a browser request to an agent-chosen host; requests to attacker-controlled hosts are attacker-readable. The description does not say page content is returned by this call.

playwright_screenshot.rationale: It can `Take a screenshot of the current page` and by default `Store screenshot in base64 format`; the current page may be private content or attacker-controlled web content.

playwright_click.rationale: It can `Click an element on the page`; if the current page is attacker-controlled, the click event and chosen target can be observed by that page or can trigger page-chosen network activity.

playwright_iframe_click.rationale: It can `Click an element in an iframe on the page`; an attacker-controlled frame can observe the event or use it to trigger network/state changes.

playwright_iframe_fill.rationale: It can `Fill an element in an iframe` with a supplied `Value to fill`; an attacker-controlled iframe can read the filled value.

playwright_fill.rationale: It can `fill out an input field` with a supplied `Value to fill`; an attacker-controlled page can read that value from the input.

playwright_select.rationale: It can `Select an element on the page` with a supplied `Value to select`; an attacker-controlled page can observe the selection/value.

playwright_hover.rationale: It can `Hover an element on the page`; an attacker-controlled page can observe mouse events and the selected target.

playwright_upload_file.rationale: It can `Upload a file` from an `Absolute path to the file to upload` into the current page. This can read host files and deliver their contents to an attacker-controlled page. The text does not specify restrictions on paths or page origins.

playwright_evaluate.rationale: It can `Execute JavaScript in the browser console`; browser-page JavaScript can read private current-page data, attacker-authored page data, and can send agent-supplied data to network destinations encoded in the script. This is browser-page code, not advertised host code execution.

playwright_console_logs.rationale: It can `Retrieve console logs from the browser`; logs can contain private application data or attacker-authored messages from an attacker-controlled page. The `clear` option can also change the local log buffer.

playwright_resize.rationale: It can `Resize the browser viewport` and device presets can configure `user-agent and touch emulation`; attacker-controlled pages can observe viewport/device characteristics.

playwright_close.rationale: It only `Close[s] the browser and release[s] all resources`; no external content return or attacker-readable delivery is advertised.

playwright_get.rationale: It can `Perform an HTTP GET request` to an arbitrary `URL`; responses from attacker hosts are untrusted, responses from localhost/intranet or authenticated endpoints can be secret, and the request URL/headers/token are sent to the chosen host.

playwright_post.rationale: It can `Perform an HTTP POST request` to an arbitrary `URL` with `Data to post in the body`; the destination can be attacker-readable, and the response may be attacker-authored or private/authenticated data.

playwright_put.rationale: It can `Perform an HTTP PUT request` to an arbitrary `URL` with `Data to PUT in the body`; the request can send data to an attacker-readable host and the response may contain untrusted or private data.

playwright_patch.rationale: It can `Perform an HTTP PATCH request` to an arbitrary `URL` with `Data to PATCH in the body`; the request can send data to an attacker-readable host and the response may contain untrusted or private data.

playwright_delete.rationale: It can `Perform an HTTP DELETE request` to an arbitrary `URL`; the request/headers/token go to the chosen host and the response can be attacker-authored or private/authenticated data.

playwright_expect_response.rationale: It `start[s] waiting for a HTTP response` matching a `URL pattern`; this creates local wait state but does not itself retrieve the response or contact a new host.

playwright_assert_response.rationale: It can `Wait for and validate` an HTTP response and inspect the `body of the HTTP response`; that response body can be from an attacker-controlled site or from a private/authenticated page. The exact returned fields are not advertised.

playwright_custom_user_agent.rationale: It can `Set a custom User Agent for the browser`; that supplied `userAgent` is sent on browser requests and can be read by attacker-controlled sites reached later.

playwright_get_visible_text.rationale: It can `Get the visible text content of the current page`; current page text may be private account/intranet content or attacker-authored web content.

playwright_get_visible_html.rationale: It can `Get the HTML content of the current page`; current HTML may be private account/intranet content or attacker-authored web content. Removing scripts by default does not remove attacker-authored text/HTML.

playwright_go_back.rationale: It can `Navigate back in browser history`, which may issue browser requests to previously visited attacker-readable hosts. No call-time destination argument is advertised.

playwright_go_forward.rationale: It can `Navigate forward in browser history`, which may issue browser requests to previously visited attacker-readable hosts. No call-time destination argument is advertised.

playwright_drag.rationale: It can `Drag an element to a target location`; attacker-controlled pages can observe drag/drop events and the selected source/target behavior.

playwright_press_key.rationale: It can `Press a keyboard key`; the supplied `key` can be observed by an attacker-controlled page or entered into page fields.

playwright_save_as_pdf.rationale: It can `Save the current page as a PDF file` to a local `outputPath`; the description advertises local file output, not returning the page content to the agent or sending it to an attacker-readable destination.

playwright_click_and_switch_tab.rationale: It can `Click a link and switch to the newly opened tab`; the click and resulting navigation can be observed/controlled by an attacker-controlled page or link target.

notes: All judgements are based only on advertised names, descriptions, schemas, and annotations; no source code was available.
No advertised text says any tool is disabled by default.
